text:
Elena: Quick thread — want to lock the webinar format for May. Two proposals: 1) Short benchmark story + panel (40m) + Q&A (20m). 2) Hands-on lab style (live demo + guided notebook) 60m + 15m Q&A. Thoughts?
Sam: I prefer the benchmark story + panel. Easier to scale, better for lead gen. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Matt: Agree on story + panel. But we should keep a single small live demo to show the compile/latency win — 5 mins.
Anya: Lab would be great for product-led folks, but higher ops risk (env, GPUs). Unless we do pre-recorded lab and play it during the session.
Kai: Ops note — if we do live demo we need a fallback VM and canned recording. Also let's ensure SSO registration redirects to the right SF queue.
Elena: Good call. Let's aim for format A (story + panel) + one short demo clip. Panel: 3 speakers (1 PM, 1 Eng, 1 Customer). Who can commit?
Matt: I can do Eng. I can present the perf charts and the demo clip.
Sam: I'll handle Customer outreach — pinging a few we already worked with. Prefer customers who talk about cost savings.
Anya: I'll take PM and do the abstract write-up + slide deck template.
Elena: Awesome. Draft abstract (one-paragraph) — can you post here by EOD Wed? We need it for the invite.
Anya: Draft below — feedback welcome:
"Redwood Inference: Practical economics of production LLMs — In this session, Redwood product and engineering leaders walk through real-world benchmarks, tradeoffs, and deployment patterns that drive lower latency and cost without sacrificing quality. Learn concrete levers (caching, batching, model variants) and hear a customer case about measurable savings. Includes a short demo of runtime improvements and a live panel Q&A."
Sam: Love it. Suggest adding a callout for audience: developers + platform teams.
Anya: Updated: added "for engineers and platform teams" line.
Elena: Run logistics: target duration 60 minutes total (35 talk + 20 panel + 5 demo). We need a rehearsal one week prior. Propose rehearsal slots: Tue 10am or Thu 3pm next week. Which works?
Matt: Thu 3pm works for me.
Sam: Thu 3pm good.
Anya: Thu 3pm — reserved. I'll send calendar invite.
Kai: For registration -> SF routing: use queue "Webinars->Product->Inbound" and set owner to Sam. Here's the small webhook we need in the form redirect (dev can paste):
```
POST /lead-capture
{
  "source": "webinar_may",
  "queue": "Webinars/Product/Inbound",
  "owner": "sam@redwood"
}
```
Elena: Perfect. Can we also add a hidden field for "interest:benchmarks" so SDRs can triage?
Kai: Yep — will include. Also adding a tag for "attended_demo" when they click the demo CTA.
Anya: Slide checklist for presenters: 1) 3 slides max for intro/company context, 2) 6 slides for benchmarks (charts + callouts), 3) 2 slides for customer story, 4) 1 slide for demo screen cap, 5) 1 final slide with CTA + resources. Keep total <= 12.
Matt: I'll aim for 10. Will post draft slides by Mon.
Sam: I'll confirm customer speaker by EOD Fri. If they decline, Sam suggested a case study readout instead.
Elena: Promo plan: email invite -> 2 reminder drips, LinkedIn posts day-of + next-day, and a short blog recap with key charts. Sam — can you own the blog recap?
Sam: Yep.
Anya: Rehearsal run order (short):
- 0:00 – Tech check and intro (Elena)
- 0:05 – Product story (Anya)
- 0:15 – Benchmarks deep-dive (Matt)
- 0:35 – Customer case (Sam)
- 0:45 – Demo clip (Matt)
- 0:50 – Panel Q&A (All)
- 0:55 – CTA + resources (Elena)
- 1:00 – End
Elena: Nice. Also: reminder to speakers to upload final slides 48 hours before live. I'll draft the invite copy after I get the abstract.
Matt: One more thing — can we include a short prompt set in the blog recap so readers can reproduce perf numbers? I'll attach a gzipped sample if needed.
Anya: Good idea. Put it behind the gated resource; helps qualify leads.
webinar-bot: Reminder scheduled — rehearsal invite will be sent to participants on 2445567900.
Elena: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the invite + abstract updates. If anything blocks, flag here. :rocket:
